I need to find the characteristic polynomial of the given matrix by computing $\det(A - \lambda I)$.

First, let me set up the matrix $A - \lambda I$:

$$A - \lambda I = \begin{pmatrix}
-4-\lambda & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10-\lambda & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14-\lambda
\end{pmatrix}$$

Now I'll compute the determinant using the first row expansion:

$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)\begin{vmatrix}
10-\lambda & 4 \\
-5 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} - (-13)\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 4 \\
12 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} + 10\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 10-\lambda \\
12 & -5
\end{vmatrix}$$

Let me compute each 2×2 determinant:

First determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
10-\lambda & 4 \\
-5 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} = (10-\lambda)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(-5) = -140-10\lambda+14\lambda+\lambda^2 + 20 = \lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120$$

Second determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 4 \\
12 & -14-\lambda
\end{vmatrix} = (-9)(-14-\lambda) - (4)(12) = 126 + 9\lambda - 48 = 78 + 9\lambda$$

Third determinant:
$$\begin{vmatrix}
-9 & 10-\lambda \\
12 & -5
\end{vmatrix} = (-9)(-5) - (10-\lambda)(12) = 45 - 120 + 12\lambda = -75 + 12\lambda$$

Now substituting back:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = (-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) + 13(78 + 9\lambda) + 10(-75 + 12\lambda)$$

Expanding the first term:
$$(-4-\lambda)(\lambda^2 + 4\lambda - 120) = -4\lambda^2 - 16\lambda + 480 - \lambda^3 - 4\lambda^2 + 120\lambda$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480$$

Expanding the other terms:
$$13(78 + 9\lambda) = 1014 + 117\lambda$$
$$10(-75 + 12\lambda) = -750 + 120\lambda$$

Combining all terms:
$$\det(A - \lambda I) = -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 104\lambda + 480 + 1014 + 117\lambda - 750 + 120\lambda$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + (104 + 117 + 120)\lambda + (480 + 1014 - 750)$$
$$= -\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744$$

Therefore, the characteristic polynomial is:

$$\boxed{-\lambda^3 - 8\lambda^2 + 341\lambda + 744}$$
